agentHost: keep WSL sessions after a successful launcher exit

Keep the WSL agent host session open when the CLI prints its ready URL and exits with code 0.
The CLI starts or reuses a detached host. Its normal exit does not mean that the host stopped.

- Keep relay leases open when the launcher exits before, during, or after relay acquisition.
- Keep failure recovery for exits before readiness, nonzero exits, signals, and process errors.
- Add lifecycle regression tests for the expected launcher behavior.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335919

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\wslRemoteAgentHostService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\wslRemoteAgentHostHelpers.test.ts` — passed, 31 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\platform\agentHost\node\wslRemoteAgentHostService.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\wslRemoteAgentHostService.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- The three successful-launcher-exit regression scenarios failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- Real Ubuntu-24.04 validation with the fixed service passed: launcher exit code 0, WebSocket
  ping/pong, shared relay leases, reconnect without another bootstrap, and relay release.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The normal detached-launcher exit was treated as backend failure, closing live relay leases and causing each recovery to repeat WSL detection and bootstrap subprocess work.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Successful WSL agent-host launches immediately lost their reusable session and forced avoidable WSL subprocess/bootstrap work and reconnection latency.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: A code-0 launcher exit after readiness no longer tears down the per-distro session or relay leases, so later connects reuse the detached host URL and avoid repeated WSL platform detection/bootstrap subprocesses.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, every child `exit` called `onChildFailure`; after the URL had produced a session, that path called `_closeSession`, disposed every relay, and forced the next `connect`/`reconnect` through `_connectUnguarded`, including `_resolvePlatform` (`wsl uname`), a new `wsl.exe` bootstrap process, and a new WebSocket. The changed guard at line 394 recognizes the launcher's documented normal code-0 exit after printing the detached host URL. The added lifecycle tests exercise exits before, during, and after relay acquisition and prove subsequent connect/reconnect reuse one spawn rather than bootstrap again.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold WSL agent-host connection through the shared process
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Renderer-to-shared-process IPC must complete platform detection, launcher bootstrap/readiness, and one localhost WebSocket handshake before the connection is usable. The changed exit guard runs only after the launcher emits exit and does not add work to this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Renderer invokes the shared-process WSL service and receives progress/relay events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical IPC connect request per caller, with same-distro bootstrap coalesced in the shared process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same proxy IPC path existed before the change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The IPC request carries the connection critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `wsl.exe ... uname` for platform detection and spawn `wsl.exe` with the bootstrap script.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One detection subprocess and one launcher subprocess per cold distro session after same-distro coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The cold connection performed the same subprocesses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both must reach URL readiness before the initial connection proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Bootstrap checks/installs/touches the remote CLI and prunes old CLI binaries inside WSL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per cold bootstrap; install/download work occurs only when the pinned CLI is missing, while touch/prune run on reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bootstrap script ran before the change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bootstrap filesystem work is on the cold connection path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the CLI on an installation miss and open the localhost WebSocket relay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one CLI download per missing installation during the coalesced bootstrap, plus one WebSocket handshake per relay lease.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same download-on-miss and per-lease WebSocket boundaries existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold install and the relay handshake block readiness.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One coalesced bootstrap per cold distro; one WebSocket per relay lease. Different distros can bootstrap independently, while concurrent callers for the same distro share `_pendingConnects`.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Platform detection and bootstrap are serialized within one per-distro connect promise; callers for that distro coalesce. Relay acquisitions may proceed concurrently after the session exists and are counted in `_pendingRelayAcquisitions`.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold cache has no `_sessions` entry and performs detection/bootstrap. Warm connects reuse the per-distro session URL. Failures are not cached; pending promises are removed in `finally`.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `_pendingConnects`, `_connectUnguarded`, the helper script, and `_createRelay` directly establish the call path and grouping.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: CLI cache-hit rate and WSL startup/download duration vary by machine, but boundary cardinality and critical-path placement are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff adds only a code-0 exit classification after readiness and does not add cold-path work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful detached launcher exit followed by additional connect or reconnect
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the URL is known, a code-0 launcher exit now returns without closing the session. A later connect/reconnect only opens a relay WebSocket against the retained URL; platform detection and bootstrap are off this warm critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open a localhost WebSocket to the detached host for each additional lease.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One handshake per effective new relay lease; reconnect calls for the same expected ID are coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A relay handshake was still needed, but normal launcher exit first destroyed the session, so recovery also repeated platform detection and launcher bootstrap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The handshake blocks that lease, but WSL detection/bootstrap no longer does.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Avoided repeat WSL platform-detection and bootstrap processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on warm reuse after the change versus a fresh detection and launcher after the old normal-exit teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every normal launcher exit entered `onChildFailure`, closed all leases/session state, and made the next connection cold-bootstrap again.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff removes subprocess work from subsequent warm connection critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective work is one retained session per active distro and one WebSocket per new relay lease, regardless of how many successful launcher-exit events occur for that single child.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The retained session is shared; concurrent relay acquisitions can open separate WebSockets, while duplicate reconnects for one expected connection ID coalesce in `_pendingReconnects`.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The `_sessions` map is the positive cache keyed by distro and remains valid through the launcher's normal exit. It is invalidated on relay acquisition failure, explicit disconnect, final lease release, service disposal, or nonzero/signal/error launcher failure.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed guard preserves `_sessions`, and added tests prove connect/reconnect use one child spawn across exits before, during, and after relay acquisition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The saved latency depends on WSL state and whether CLI installation is already warm; the removed subprocess count is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improvement, not a regression. The concrete repeated-bootstrap fix was recorded with introducing commit provenance.

Scenarios.Scenario: Host or relay failure after the detached launcher has exited
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A physical WebSocket close notifies the reconnecting transport. Reconnect first checks running distros, then attempts a WebSocket against the retained session URL; connection-refused retries are bounded by the existing 30-second open deadline. On failure `_createRelay` closes the stale session, allowing a later attempt to cold-bootstrap.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe `wsl --list --running --quiet` before reconnect and, after stale-session invalidation on a later attempt, perform platform detection/bootstrap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One running-state probe per reconnect attempt; cold bootstrap occurs once after stale session removal, coalesced per distro.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The reconnect probe and bootstrap path already existed; before this fix, the normal launcher exit had already removed the session and forced bootstrap immediately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The probe and any eventual bootstrap block recovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retry localhost WebSocket establishment against the retained URL with linear backoff capped at 500 ms and a 30-second total deadline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded retry loop per effective reconnect, coalesced for duplicate expected connection IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same retry policy existed; the old normal-exit bug generally removed the session before a later reconnect could reuse it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The retry loop can delay stale-endpoint recovery, but it is the pre-existing bounded policy that also tolerates WSL forwarding startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One running-distro probe and one bounded WebSocket retry sequence per reconnect attempt; duplicate reconnects for the same connection ID coalesce. Cost does not scale with output history, and buffered launcher output is capped at 50 lines.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-connection reconnect promises coalesce by expected ID, but independent relay IDs can reconnect concurrently. The diff does not alter the existing retry loop or aggregate limiter behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The retained positive session is invalidated when relay acquisition fails. There is no negative cache; a later attempt can create a fresh session. Launcher output retention remains bounded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the reconnect path and 30-second bound; lower for real-world frequency of detached-host-only crashes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A detached host crash while its WSL distro remains running is less common than normal launcher exit, and whether localhost forwarding recovers within the deadline depends on the failure mode.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The retry is bounded, coalesced, and pre-existing, and the diff replaces an immediate, unconditional teardown that already made the successful-launch workflow unusable rather than moving a previously healthy recovery onto a slower path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Final relay release, explicit disconnect, or service shutdown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Release crosses IPC, closes the WebSocket synchronously in the shared process, and when no acquisitions or leases remain disposes the session. Because the launcher already exited successfully, `_killChild` returns immediately; the detached host self-cleans via its 300-second idle timeout off the release critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Renderer releases the relay lease in the shared process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per relay ID due renderer-side released/in-flight deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same release IPC and deduplication existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: IPC dispatch precedes local cleanup; detached-host idle shutdown is off path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same WebSocket close occurred before the change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local close is part of release; no new handshake or remote call is added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potentially signal the launcher child during session close; after a successful code-0 exit `_killChild` observes the recorded exit code and does not signal or schedule escalation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One check per closed session, with zero signal calls for the successful detached-launcher case.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same child-state check existed, but the session was often closed prematurely at normal launcher exit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No subprocess wait blocks release; detached host idle cleanup is asynchronous and remote.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cleanup is linear in leases belonging to the one session during explicit session close; normal final release handles one lease. Retained session state is bounded by active distros and leases.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pending relay acquisition prevents premature session close. Session disposal owns child listeners, and explicit service disposal iterates current connections and sessions once.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Final lease release invalidates the distro session. No session remains cached without a lease or pending acquisition; the remote detached process has its own bounded idle lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `_closeRelay`, `_canCloseSession`, `_closeSession`, and `_killChild` explicitly define ownership and cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The detached host's actual post-release shutdown time can be up to its configured 300-second idle timeout, but that bounded remote lifetime existed in the launch command and is not extended by retained local state after final release.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Listener/session cleanup remains owned and bounded, and the diff does not retain local session state after the final lease.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all two changed files and their complete diff pages. The production guard correctly distinguishes the detached launcher's normal exit, removing repeated WSL bootstrap work. Tests only add bounded lifecycle coverage. No diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold; one concrete repeated-work regression fix was recorded.
